variants.headline: {{cityName}} completes the {{building}}
body: The {{building}} in {{cityName}} is finished, raised by the city's own masons and carpenters rather than bought with coin. From this week the city can put it to use.

variants.headline: Notice from {{cityName}}: the {{building}} is ready
body: Notice is given that the {{building}} at {{cityName}} stands finished and ready for use from this week on.

variants.headline: The scaffolding comes down in {{cityName}}
body: The fences came down this week, and the {{building}} stood finished behind them. The men who had watched it rise since the first post went in lingered a while, as if the show were not over. In {{cityName}} the talk has moved from waiting to using.

variants.headline: What the finished {{building}} says about {{cityName}}
body: The {{building}} is finished in {{cityName}}, and the completion makes two statements. One concerns the building itself. The other concerns a city with the surplus, the hands and the patience to see long work through, and that is the statement rivals read closest. A finished work is also a promise of the next one.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} puts money behind the {{building}}
body: Extra coin has gone into the {{building}} at {{cityName}}, laid down to hurry the work along. The building rises the faster for it, and the city will have it sooner.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} funds the {{building}}
body: We are given to understand that {{cityName}} has laid fresh money on the {{building}}, and that the work proceeds the quicker for it. The sums stand committed.

variants.headline: Why {{cityName}} is paying for the {{building}}
body: Extra money is going into the {{building}} at {{cityName}}, and the reason is time: the city would rather have the building soon than the gold in hand. Whether the trade was wise will show in the treasury, and in whatever the city could not buy with the coin it spent.

variants.headline: Hear it, {{cityName}}! Coin speeds the {{building}}
body: Hear it, good people! Money is laid down for the {{building}}, and the work goes forward the faster! The {{building}} comes sooner. The {{building}} comes sooner!

variants.headline: {{cityName}} buys the {{building}}
body: The {{building}} is finished in {{cityName}}, paid for outright in {{currency}}. There was no construction to wait through; the building is ready for use now.

variants.headline: No wait in {{cityName}}: the {{building}} is bought
body: Other cities watch brick rise on brick for years. {{cityName}} counted out {{currency}} instead, and the {{building}} opened its doors while the ink on the receipt was drying.

variants.headline: A purchase for {{cityName}}: the {{building}} is ready
body: We are advised that {{cityName}} has secured the {{building}} with {{currency}}, a prompt piece of business that reflects credit on the city's officers. The building stands ready for use from this day.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} pays for speed
body: There was no scaffolding to take down at the {{building}} in {{cityName}}: the city paid in {{currency}} and took it finished. What the purchase saved was time, and what it cost sits in the treasury. Which mattered more will show in what the city does with the building it now has.

variants.headline: {{largest}} outgrows the capital
body: The realm's largest city is no longer its capital. {{largest}} counts {{largestPopulation}} people, more than {{capital}}.

variants.headline: {{largest}} pass the capital
body: {{largest}} each count {{largestPopulation}} people, and every one of them has outgrown {{capital}}. The capital now looks up at more cities than one.

variants.headline: {{largest}} now outweighs {{capital}}
body: {{largest}} has passed {{capital}} in population, and the realm has quietly shifted its weight. Government keeps its address in {{capital}}, but the nation's people now mostly live elsewhere, and a nation's business tends in time to follow its people. The seat of power has not moved. The center of the realm has.

variants.headline: {{capital}} loses its crown to {{largest}}
body: The corner orators of {{capital}} have had to retire their favorite opening line. {{largest}} counts {{largestPopulation}} people now, and the biggest crowds in the realm gather somewhere else. The orators still draw a crowd, it should be said. Just not the biggest one.

variants.headline: The capital just got outgrown
body: {{largest}} has passed {{capital}}: {{largestPopulation}} people and counting. The government stays in the capital. The crowds are in {{largest}} now.

variants.headline: The same grievance in {{count}} cities
body: In {{count}} of our cities, the leading complaint is the same one: {{key}}. A trouble that appears in that many places at once is no longer any single city's affair.

variants.headline: One problem, {{count}} cities
body: {{key}} now leads the complaints in {{count}} of our cities at once, which is past the point where bad luck explains it. One city's trouble can be misfortune. The same trouble in every quarter is a pattern, and a pattern has an author somewhere in the government's choices.

variants.headline: Hunger in {{count}} of our cities
body: Famine tops the grievance list in {{count}} of our cities now. Ask anyone in the bread lines: this stopped being one city's hard luck a while back.

variants.headline: Boredom in {{count}} cities
body: In {{count}} of our cities the complaint is the same: nothing to do once the work is done. The evenings stretch long, the squares stand quiet, and everyone has heard every story twice.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} is being razed
body: {{civilization}} has put {{cityName}} to the torch. {{turns}} turns remain before nothing is left of it but the ground it stood on.

variants.headline: A city we cannot name is burning
body: A city is burning under {{civilization}}'s hand, and its name has not even reached us. {{turns}} turns remain before there is nothing left to name.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} burns with {{population}} people inside
body: {{civilization}} is razing {{cityName}} with {{population}} people inside its walls. {{turns}} turns remain before the city and its inhabitants are gone.

variants.headline: A city burns {{distance}} tiles from our nearest city
body: Letters from the frontier relate that {{civilization}} is putting {{cityName}} to the torch, just {{distance}} tiles from our own settlements. The glow on the horizon is near enough to watch.

variants.headline: The end of {{cityName}}
body: In {{turns}} turns, {{cityName}} will pass from the map entire: its walls, its markets and its prayers ending together. {{civilization}} has chosen that nothing stand where the city stood, and so nothing will.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} is ours
body: Our forces have taken {{cityName}} from {{formerOwner}}, and the city passes under our flag with its walls, its people and its grain.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} is ours
body: Our forces have taken {{cityName}}. Whose banner flew over it yesterday is not recorded in the dispatches; ours flies over it now.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} falls to {{captor}}
body: {{captor}} has taken {{cityName}} from us. The city stands under a foreign flag now, and its people with it.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} is lost
body: The flag above {{cityName}} is no longer ours. Who holds the city now is unclear; the loss itself is beyond doubt.

variants.headline: A city changes hands
body: A city has changed hands, and the hand that won or lost it was ours. The dispatches name no streets and no gates, but its people woke this morning under a flag that was not flying over them yesterday.

variants.headline: What {{cityName}} adds
body: {{cityName}} is ours, and so is the ground it commands. The taking adds the city's people, its works and its walls, and it pushes our frontier onto land that must now be held. Strength took the city; strength will keep it.

variants.headline: Citizens, {{cityName}} deserved better
body: {{cityName}} is gone, and its people answer to another flag. The government will call it a loss of territory; we call it a loss that somebody's decisions failed to prevent. Name the failure before the next city pays for it.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} finishes new defenses
body: Work on the {{building}} at {{cityName}} is done, and the city is a harder target than it was.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} strengthens its walls
body: The {{building}} at {{cityName}} is complete. Any army that comes this way will find the city a harder prize than its map suggests.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} is ready for a siege
body: Hear it, people of {{cityName}}! The {{building}} stands complete. Our walls are the stronger for it. Our walls are the stronger!

variants.headline: A stronger {{cityName}}
body: We are advised that the {{building}} at {{cityName}} is complete, the council's provision for the city's safety standing finished. {{cityName}} rests tonight behind stouter walls, and the foresight belongs where it was earned.

variants.headline: Famine grips {{city}}
body: Hunger now outweighs every other trouble in {{city}}. On the city's own count, {{famine}} of its discontent comes down to empty bellies.

variants.headline: Why {{city}} is hungry
body: Famine stands first among {{city}}'s grievances, measured at {{famine}} on the city's own count. Feeding the city is the first duty of any government, and on that measure the present one is coming up short.

variants.headline: Empty stalls in {{city}}
body: The bread sellers of {{city}} set out half what they used to, and the queue forms before the stalls are even open. Hunger leads the city's grievances now, and everyone in that queue can say why.

variants.headline: A call for bread in {{city}}
body: Famine weighs on {{city}} above every other trouble, and the city's stores and its people both stand in need. Let the faithful open their granaries to their neighbors, for charity in a hungry season is worth more than any fast.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} changes allegiance
body: {{cityName}} has left {{formerOwner}} to join {{newOwner}}. The city made the change by its own decision, with no army at its gates.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} chooses a new flag
body: Cities change hands by conquest or by choice, and the two are not the same kind of event. {{cityName}} has gone from {{formerOwner}} to {{newOwner}} without a battle, which means the new flag was invited in. Invitations can be withdrawn.

variants.headline: Madam, we are {{newOwner}} now
body: The flag over our square changed this week: {{formerOwner}}'s down, {{newOwner}}'s up. We, the people of {{cityName}}, are the same people underneath it. Trade with us as before, govern us with courtesy, and you will find us the neighbors we always were.

variants.headline: The flag changed overnight in {{cityName}}
body: The night watch in {{cityName}} went to bed under {{formerOwner}}'s colors and woke to {{newOwner}}'s. Nobody fired a shot. The baker opened at his usual hour and sold to the usual faces, and the only change on the street was the cloth above it.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} reaches {{population}} people
body: {{cityName}} counts {{population}} people, crossing the mark that makes it a {{milestone}} in our realm.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} crosses {{population}}
body: {{cityName}} has reached {{population}} people, the measure of a {{milestone}}, and the city now grows in a new way: more people need more fields, more work and more room, and a city that supplies them draws the families that make the next milestone. The next few seasons will show which kind of city {{cityName}} means to be.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} has grown to {{population}}!
body: Hear it, good people! {{cityName}} now numbers {{population}} souls, and is counted a {{milestone}} among our cities. Say it loud: a {{milestone}} is among us!

variants.headline: A milestone for {{cityName}}
body: A city grows slowly, and the growing counts. {{cityName}} now numbers {{population}} people, the measure of a {{milestone}}, and takes an established place among the cities of the realm, with the burdens that established places carry.

variants.headline: {{liberator}} liberates {{liberated}}
body: {{liberated}} has been restored to independence by {{liberator}}. A nation that was held under another's banner answers to its own flag again.

variants.headline: Our independence is restored
body: Occupation is ended. {{liberator}} has returned our nation to its own flag, and we answer to ourselves again.

variants.headline: {{liberated}} is free again
body: Our forces have restored {{liberated}} to its independence. The nation that was held under another's banner flies its own colors today.

variants.headline: A nation restored: {{liberated}} is free
body: By the hand of {{liberator}}, {{liberated}} has resumed its place among the independent nations of the world, to the satisfaction of all who wish their neighbors well.

variants.headline: Freedom for {{liberated}}
body: {{liberated}} stands free, and {{liberator}} holds the credit. A power that restores a nation wins a name that garrisons cannot buy, and this paper counts the deed worth more than any ground taken in war.

variants.headline: Pillaged land weighs on {{city}}
body: Raided fields and broken roads are the heaviest burden in {{city}}. The city puts {{pillaged}} of its discontent down to the stripped ground outside the walls.

variants.headline: The fields around {{city}} lie in ruin
body: Pillage tops the grievance list in {{city}}, measured at {{pillaged}} on the city's count. The raiders ride away and the broken fields remain, and repair is a cost somebody in the capital has yet to answer for.

variants.headline: The road to {{city}} is empty now
body: The road into {{city}} used to fill at dawn with carts bound for market. The fields along it stand stripped now, and the city names pillage as its heaviest complaint.

variants.headline: {{city}} counts the cost of pillage
body: The city of {{city}} attributes {{pillaged}} of its discontent to pillaged land, the largest single cause, and the damage lies outside the walls. Repair will want many hands, and the city asks its neighbors for the loan of some.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} is under siege
body: Enemy forces have ringed {{cityName}}, and the walls have taken real damage. The city holds, and the siege goes on.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} holds against the siege
body: Hear it, people of {{cityName}}! The enemy stands at the gates, and the city has not fallen. The walls stand at {{hitPoints}} of {{maxHitPoints}}. Hold fast! The walls hold! The walls hold!

variants.headline: The siege of {{cityName}} tests the frontier
body: A siege is a test of supply before it is a test of walls. While {{cityName}} is surrounded, the city burns through stores and time it cannot quickly replace, and relief, whenever it comes, will be somebody's decision to explain.

variants.headline: Life inside besieged {{cityName}}
body: Inside {{cityName}} the market stalls stand half empty and the talk runs quiet. The siege is not news from the frontier here; it is the sound at the gate in every hour of the night.

variants.headline: The defense of {{cityName}} continues
body: We are advised that {{cityName}} remains under siege. The garrison holds the walls, which stand at {{hitPoints}} of {{maxHitPoints}}, and the city's commanders describe the defense as steady and the stores as sufficient.

variants.headline: A new colony {{distance}} tiles from the capital
body: Our settlers have founded {{cityName}}, {{distance}} tiles out from the capital. The colony must stand on its own for a while, the capital being a long way behind it.

variants.headline: A colony far from the capital
body: A new settlement stands {{distance}} tiles from the capital, farther than any of our present towns. Its name has not yet reached us.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} is a long way from home
body: {{cityName}} lies {{distance}} tiles from the capital, an outpost by any measure. Distance will tax its supply and its defense, but the site now flies our flag, and the empty land between it and home will not stay empty for long.

variants.headline: A new town, {{distance}} tiles out
body: The nation has a new colony at {{cityName}}, {{distance}} tiles from the capital. We wish the settlers well. We note, as ever, that frontiers are exciting for those who do not have to pay for them.

variants.headline: A colony at {{cityName}}
body: Advice reaches us of a new settlement: {{cityName}}, founded {{distance}} tiles from the capital. The colony begins with little beyond its site and the courage of the people who chose it.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} completes the {{building}} in {{cityName}}
body: The {{building}} at {{cityName}}, a city of {{civilization}} near our borders, is finished. The building now serves the city that raised it.

variants.headline: New work near our border
body: {{civilization}} has completed the {{building}} in one of its cities near our border. The city's name has not reached us; the finished work stands close enough all the same.

variants.headline: New works at {{cityName}}
body: The {{building}} is finished at {{cityName}}, and {{civilization}} can now put it to use. A work this close to our border changes what a neighbor can bring to bear here. Whatever our answer is, it should assume the neighbor is not finished building.

variants.headline: From beyond our border: {{cityName}} completes the {{building}}
body: Word arrives from across the border that {{cityName}}, a city of {{civilization}}, has completed the {{building}}. We record the work for what it says of our neighbor's industry.

variants.headline: A neighbor's new work
body: Travelers crossing the border bring the same account: the scaffolding down at {{cityName}}, and the {{building}} open behind it. The work was done quietly, and the news of it arrived after the fact.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} buys the {{building}} in {{cityName}}
body: The {{building}} at {{cityName}} is ready for use. {{civilization}} paid in {{currency}} rather than wait for the work to run its course.

variants.headline: A purchase near our border
body: {{civilization}} has bought the {{building}} outright, paying in {{currency}} in a city near our border whose name has not reached us.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} pays for the {{building}} near our border
body: The {{building}} at {{cityName}} was bought, not built: {{civilization}} paid for it finished. A neighbor with money to spare for haste is worth watching, and this one is close.

variants.headline: A neighbor's deep purse
body: The traders from {{cityName}} tell one story: one season a fenced building site, the next an open door. The {{building}} arrived finished, because {{civilization}} paid in {{currency}} and skipped the waiting.

variants.headline: Notice from {{cityName}}: the {{building}} is bought
body: It is learned that {{civilization}} has purchased the {{building}} at {{cityName}}, the account settled in {{currency}}. The work, we understand, was bought complete rather than raised over time.

variants.headline: A new town on the doorstep of {{ours}}
body: {{player}} has founded {{city}}, {{distance}} tiles from {{ours}}. Two towns this close share one stretch of ground between them.

variants.headline: A rival town rises close to home
body: {{player}} has planted a town {{distance}} tiles from one of our cities. What was open ground between us is now their street and their claim.

variants.headline: {{player}} plants a town near {{ours}}
body: {{city}} stands {{distance}} tiles from {{ours}}, inside ground both nations could use. {{player}} will call it a town; a planner of wars calls it a stake driven into shared land, and the stake is theirs.

variants.headline: {{city}} rises beside {{ours}}
body: {{player}} has founded {{city}} {{distance}} tiles from {{ours}}, and the ground our farmers cross is suddenly a frontier. This paper wants the border surveyed and marked before the next planting season, because fields that two nations use become incidents faster than either notices.

variants.headline: New neighbors at {{city}}
body: We learn that {{player}} has founded {{city}}, {{distance}} tiles from {{ours}}. A border this near will test both nations' manners, but a neighboring town also brings new customers within easy reach of our merchants.

variants.headline: {{city}} comes under direct rule
body: The same flag flies over {{city}}, but its time as a puppet is ended. The city now answers to the direct government of {{owner}}.

variants.headline: {{owner}} tightens its hold on {{city}}
body: {{city}} has passed from puppet rule to the direct government of {{owner}}, at a site {{distance}} tiles from our own cities. The realm next door has tightened its grip within sight of our borders.

variants.headline: A puppet no more: {{city}} answers to {{owner}}
body: {{owner}} now rules {{city}} directly, and the change is not ceremonial. Puppets hesitate; provinces march. A neighbor that can now call on this city's men and grain is a different neighbor than it was.

variants.headline: A change of rule in {{city}}
body: Notice is given of a change of station at {{city}}: the city, lately governed as a puppet, now answers to {{owner}} directly. The formality is small; the meaning is not.

variants.headline: Resistance continues in {{cityName}}
body: {{cityName}} remains under occupation, and the city has not accepted it. Resistance is expected to last {{turns}} more turns before {{cityName}} answers our orders.

variants.headline: Resistance continues in an occupied city
body: One of the cities we hold under occupation continues to resist our rule. {{turns}} more turns are expected before its administration answers to us.

variants.headline: {{population}} people in an occupied {{cityName}}
body: On paper, {{cityName}} is ours: {{population}} people added to the realm with the stroke of a mapmaker. In practice the city resists, and {{turns}} turns of it lie ahead. Conquest counts the taking; it cannot count the agreeing.

variants.headline: The old loyalty runs deep in {{cityName}}
body: A fruit seller in {{cityName}} was heard pricing her figs in {{formerOwner}}'s coin this week. The city is not reconciled to its new ruler, and the resistance runs on: {{turns}} more turns by the reckoning.

variants.headline: Mood darkens in occupied {{cityName}}
body: Occupation weighs on {{cityName}}, and the city's own books count the mood of its streets at {{unrest}}. Resistance is expected to run {{turns}} more turns before the city settles under our flag.

variants.headline: A new city: {{cityName}}
body: Our settlers have founded {{cityName}}, and a new city stands under our flag. The work begins now: first houses, first fields, first walls.

variants.headline: A new city is founded
body: Our settlers have founded a new city. The ground is ours, the name is not yet in the records, and the work of building begins.

variants.headline: Hear it! {{cityName}} is founded
body: Hear it, good people! Our settlers have founded {{cityName}}, and a new city stands on the map of the realm. Carry the name abroad: {{cityName}}!

variants.headline: {{cityName}} begins its story
body: {{cityName}} begins with a site, some settlers and a claim. What it becomes depends on what the nation sends next: people, grain, tools, patience. Every great city of the realm started exactly this small.

variants.headline: A new settlement at {{cityName}}
body: We are pleased to record that our settlers have founded {{cityName}}. The new town begins under the nation's protection, with the government's intentions for its care said to be settled and generous.

variants.headline: Settlers ready as {{town}} grows smaller
body: A party of settlers is ready to leave {{town}}, and the city is smaller for the making of it. Fewer mouths remain to feed, and there is food to spare for the ones who stay.

variants.headline: Settlers ready, spirits low in {{town}}
body: {{town}} has raised a party of settlers and given up part of its people to do it. The bread stretches further now, yet the city's mood has gone the other way, and no one in charge has explained why.

variants.headline: Good cheer in {{town}} as settlers prepare to go
body: A party of settlers is ready to leave {{town}}, and the city sends them off in good heart. With fewer at the tables there is more on each plate, and the city's mood has risen with its prospects.

variants.headline: One fewer place at supper in {{town}}
body: The supper tables of {{town}} have {{lost}} empty places this week, and the families who filled them are off to found a city somewhere. There is more bread to go around now, and fewer hands to bake it.

variants.headline: {{city}} is eating into its stores
body: {{city}} raises less food than it eats. Against a store of {{foodStored}} and a shortfall of {{shortfall}} each turn, the arithmetic ends one way, and it ends with empty granaries.

variants.headline: Why {{city}} is starving in peacetime
body: No enemy sits outside {{city}}, and the city is hungry all the same, losing {{shortfall}} food a turn against a store of {{foodStored}}. In wartime, hunger has an obvious author. In peace it has a planner, and the planner is nowhere to be seen.

variants.headline: The granary at {{city}} is emptying
body: The bakers of {{city}} have started counting loaves instead of selling them. The store stands at {{foodStored}} and falls by {{shortfall}} a turn, and there is no army outside the walls to blame for a single crumb of it.

variants.headline: The food account of {{city}}
body: Stores: {{foodStored}}.
Shortfall: {{shortfall}} each turn.
Besieged: no. At war: no. The account closes on hunger all the same.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} is being razed
body: Our forces have put {{cityName}} to the torch. {{turns}} turns remain before the city is gone and the site lies bare.

variants.headline: A city is being razed
body: Our forces are burning a city whose name has not reached this paper. {{turns}} turns remain of it.

variants.headline: The decision to raze {{cityName}}
body: In {{turns}} turns, {{cityName}} will be gone from the map, leaving nothing to garrison, feed or govern. The realm keeps the ground and sheds the burden, and the decision that made it so was ours alone.

variants.headline: The end of {{cityName}}
body: {{cityName}} has {{turns}} turns left, and then only the ground it stood on. Whatever the city was, its walls will keep no record of it. May the gods it prayed to remember what the fire will not.

variants.headline: {{population}} people and {{turns}} turns left in {{cityName}}
body: {{population}} people remain in {{cityName}} as the fires take it. In {{turns}} turns the site will be empty, and the roads out of the city are the busiest streets it has now.
